items.title: Powers of an element of the Jacobson radical of the integral closure of a one-dimensional semi-local domain land back in the domain
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma records that the integral closure B' of a semi-local Noetherian one-dimensional domain B in its fraction field is a semi-local Dedekind domain, and that for a nonzero x in the Jacobson radical of B' and any y in B' some power x^n y lies in B. The proof builds the subring A generated by B, x and y inside B', shows it is finite over B, observes that the finite module A/B is supported on the closed points of B so that a power of the Jacobson radical of B lands in B, notes that Spec(B') -> Spec(A) is surjective and hence A is semi-local with x in its Jacobson radical, and finishes with x^m y in m_B A for some m, giving x^{nm} y in B (proof lines 7427-7443). H2: the intermediate ring A and the two-step use of the conductor to absorb y are the substance.
